feature.name: Client Redux Toolkit migration
feature.summary: Replace three Zustand stores while preserving all current client behavior.

domain.process: authenticate, create and read a project
invariants: provider tokens and raw errors absent from state and actions

orchestration.user workflows: model commands and per-instance RTK listener middleware

state_transitions: auth cancel -> signed-out; pause preserves visible outcome
valid submit -> submitting -> saved or editing with retained draft
read -> saved/missing/failure; 401 clears cache and returns to sign-in
interrupted create -> editing with uncertainty warning; manual retry only

public_contracts: preserve factory parameters and command methods
expose stores only through getState and subscribe
internal_contracts: private createSlice reducers with semantic serializable actions
createListenerMiddleware per model, prepended to defaults
predicate compares current.operation and previous.operation identity
controllers and operation generation remain per-model closure state

transport: existing separate client User and ProjectDefinition wire contracts

application: signed-in actor and editable status before create

concurrency.state_owner: one private store per factory representation
concurrency.ordering: synchronous intent transition and listener start; async completion freshness checks
concurrency.idempotency: duplicate pending submits suppressed; no server create idempotency claim
concurrency.cancellation: abort controller plus generation, actor and route checks; facade checks immediately before cache write; disposal unregisters own listener
concurrency.partial_failure: retain existing warning that interrupted create may have saved

static_analysis: no Zustand imports or active dependency entries
private mutation surfaces and real RTK listeners
architecture_tests: non-operation transitions do not retrigger requests
boundary_tests: stale/aborted completions cannot write cache or navigate

contracts: mounted React updates and preserved focus/history verified by QA

tradeoffs: three model-local stores preserve existing ownership
native whole-snapshot React subscriptions avoid new binding dependency

deferred: existing unused project state stubs remain untouched
